resources.string: Combines a left and right Joy-Con into one virtual controller and hides the originals from other apps.
Shizuku is not running. Start it in the Shizuku app, then come back.
Shizuku permission was denied. Allow Merge Controller in the Shizuku app.
%1$s: not connected. Pair it in Bluetooth settings.
Stopped. The Joy-Cons work as separate controllers.
Running as “%1$s”. Waiting for the Joy-Cons: press any button on each to connect it.
Off: face buttons map by position, like Android does for Joy-Cons (bottom button = A). On: they map by label (the button marked A = A).

Uses the name, IDs and button layout of an Xbox Wireless Controller, so games that only accept known controllers (like Call of Duty: Mobile) recognize it. Changing this recreates the merged controller.
Rumble sent to the merged controller is passed on over Bluetooth: the strong motor to the left Joy-Con, the weak motor to the right.
Listed before the Joy-Cons, so games that use the first controller (like GTA: San Andreas) will pick it.
Listed after the Joy-Cons. Games that use the first controller (like GTA: San Andreas) will ignore it. Reconnect the Joy-Cons to fix this.
Press buttons while this screen is open. When merging, every event should come from the merged controller.

Left stick x %1$+.2f y %2$+.2f
Right stick z %3$+.2f rz %4$+.2f
Triggers L %5$.2f R %6$.2f
D-pad (hat) x %7$+.0f y %8$+.0f
Without root, Android still lists the original Joy-Cons, but while merging they send no input to any app.
